points.description: States the new steady-state error is zero (θss = θd, for any θd), with the cancellation of the gravity term shown or clearly asserted (the added +mgℓ sinθ cancels the plant's gravity term, leaving J θ̈ + (b+Kd) θ̇ + Kp(θ−θd) = 0). A bare 'zero' with no mention of cancellation earns no marks.

Correct, justified statement about the closed-loop poles. Award the mark for either: (a) the general answer: the poles do change, because the gravity stiffness term mgℓcosθ is removed from the s-coefficient/stiffness term (compensated: s² + ((b+Kd)/J)s + Kp/J, versus (Kp+mgℓcosθ)/J before); or (b) the specific answer: at θd = 90° the gravity stiffness mgℓcosθ is zero or very small, so the poles are essentially unchanged at this operating point, though they would change elsewhere. Both together is the best answer (no extra marks; marker should note it on the script). No mark for an unjustified 'yes' or 'no', or for 'poles change because the plant is now linear' without identifying which coefficient (the mgℓcosθ stiffness) changes.

rubric.notes: Each point is worth 1 mark, all or nothing. P1 needs zero error plus cancellation of gravity. P2 needs a justified pole statement identifying the mgℓcosθ stiffness term, either the general 'poles change' or the 'negligible at 90°' version.
